transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… good to meet you too. I guess what’s been bothering me is I’m having a harder time keeping things in order at work. I work with customer tickets and receipts and notes, and lately they all sort of end up in piles together. Then I’m standing there not really knowing which job I’m supposed to handle first. It sounds silly, maybe, but it’s been getting in the way.
Have you had this kind of trouble staying organized ever since you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I did fine enough, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but even in grade school my teachers would tell my mom I was bright, just kind of… scattered. They’d say I talked out of turn, lost papers, and needed reminders to finish my work. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often feel unusually restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m causing a scene or anything, but I do have a hard time just staying put sometimes. Like during church committee meetings, or those fabric-care trainings at work, I’ll find little reasons to get up—get water, grab papers, check on something—even when everyone else is still sitting. I guess I feel better if I’m moving a little. Is that what you mean?
Do these difficulties with staying organized and focused happen outside of work too?

Yes… it does, though I maybe don’t talk about that as much. At church, I used to help lead some planning things, and I’ve kind of stepped back from that because people were getting frustrated with me when I’d miss details or not have things straight.

And at the shop it’s caused some real problems too—late orders, mixed-up billing, awkward moments with the staff or customers. I don’t mean to make it sound dramatic, but it’s not just at work, no.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized or wired for several days in a row?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I have days where I’m busy or wound up, like anyone, but not several days where I felt unusually wired in a way that stood out to me. At least, nothing I’d know to call that. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

I’m not sure I’d say “a lot,” exactly. I mean, I worry about normal things—work, family, whether I’ve forgotten something—but I don’t know that it comes out of nowhere with no reason. Maybe I get concerned when there’s something actually going on. Is that the kind of worry you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I don’t think I’d say depressed, no. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but lately I haven’t noticed feeling really down in that way. I’m okay, I think… unless you mean something more specific?
Has your trouble with focus and organization gotten noticeably worse recently compared with how you’ve usually been?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it has been more of a real problem the last couple years. Maybe about two years and a couple months, since I started changing the business into this more complicated boutique kind of model. Before that I managed okay, mostly, but since then the focus and organizing part has been harder to keep up with.
Have you been having trouble with your memory lately?

Memory? Um… I don’t think so, not in a serious way. I mean, I might forget little things here and there, but I kind of feel like everybody does that. I haven’t noticed anything that feels really alarming, unless there’s something specific you mean by memory trouble?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern since childhood of disorganization, losing papers, needing reminders to finish work, talking out of turn, and current restlessness with difficulty remaining seated. Symptoms occur across settings (work and church) and cause clear functional impairment, especially occupational problems and interpersonal frustration. Bipolar-spectrum, anxiety, depressive, and memory-based explanations were not supported in the interview.
